thread:
mira: Heads up — noticed canary nodes started hitting OOM kills around 11:12 UTC. Symptoms: sudden KV cache eviction spikes, large batches forming with very long prefixes, and the kernel-router dropping to the slower fp32 path. perf-bot posted a pprof. :grimacing:

jon: link? do we have a flamegraph or heap profile?

perf-bot: pprof links -> heap: https://perf.example/pprof/5332109876/heap , cpu: https://perf.example/pprof/5332109876/cpu :chart_with_upwards_trend:

mira: quick snippets from the heap report — KV resident set jumped from ~9MB -> ~28MB per shard within 3m. eviction rate ~420/s. batch size median tokens rose from 120 -> 820. tail latency spiked.

sarah: hmm that token median is wild. Any obvious request pattern change? long context vs reranks?

mira: traffic is normal, but there's an uptick in a few customers sending long prompts (avg 3k tokens) + heavy streaming sessions. The batcher is greedily packing prefixes which exacerbates KV footprint.

lee: kernel side — kernel-router log during the window shows many kernel handoffs where quantized kernels refused due to 'kv_mem_estimate > 12MB' heuristic, so route picked fp32 fallback. FP32 kernels blow memory and increase per-request KV caching.

jon: can we short-circuit greedy batch assembly under high-KV pressure? i.e. enforce token-budget per-queue and favor earlier admits rather than waiting for a big pack.

mira: agreed. I ran a micro-experiment on a canary shard: lowered batch_token_target from 8192 -> 3072 and added a soft kv_headroom reserve. Results: OOMs stopped, eviction rate down ~70%, p50 latency ~ +10ms, p99 down ~120ms. Good tradeoff.

sarah: nice. Do you have the config diff?

mira: pasted the minimal patch we used:
```yaml
batcher:
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  token_target: 3072  # lowered target to reduce greedy packing
  batch_timeout_ms: 6
  kv_eviction_reserve_bytes: 1048576  # 1MB per shard soft reserve
  preemptive_admit_threshold: 0.75  # admit earlier when cache pressure is high
kernel_router:
  prefer_quant_kernels_under_mem_frac: 0.6  # be willing to pick quant kernels if mem usage <60%
  fallthrough_latency_penalty_ms: 8
```

lee: subtle but important: prefer_quant_kernels_under_mem_frac avoids the strict >12MB cutover which was too coarse. We should compute kv_mem_estimate relative to device memory (frac) not absolute bytes.

jon: also suggest adding a transient token_budget per-queue that decays — when eviction_rate > X, reduce token_budget by 50% for next N batches. Lightweight control loop, no need to change hard limits.

mira: implemented a simple PID-ish reducer in the batcher: if eviction_rate > 200/s for 10s -> token_target *= 0.5 for 30s, then linear warmback. On canary this smoothed peaks.

perf-bot: quick numbers from the canary run (10m window): eviction_rate 420->120/s, avg batch tokens 820->280, avg kernel handoffs reduced 3.8->1.1, p99 latency -115ms.

sarah: great. Any regression risk? lowering batch token_target could increase per-token compute cost. We need to run cost/latency instrumentation over 24h before roll.

lee: kernel selection change has a potential regression: if quant kernel is used but numeric mismatch causes slight accuracy drift for some ops. We must gate by model QC tests.

mira: action plan: (1) extend canary window to 24h with the new batcher + kernel_router flags (owner: mira), (2) add automated QC eval against 10 critical prompts to detect quantization drift (owner: lee), (3) add metric alert for eviction_rate > 250/s and token_target scaling events (owner: jon).

jon: I'll also put a temporary throttle on the router so batches above 6k tokens are split earlier — cheap mitigation while we validate.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for shard=canary-7 with cfg=kv-pressure-slim.json. ETA ~ 2m. :rocket:

mira: thanks. If canary looks stable for 24h we can roll to the rest with a staged ramp + cost telemetry.

sarah: small doc note: we should add a short section in the batching heuristics doc about "kv-aware admission" and include the PID-style token_target backoff. I can PR after canary.

lee: also add a kernel_router test that asserts prefer_quant_kernels_under_mem_frac doesn't flip on for models marked quant-unsafe.

mira: perfect. I'll post a summary in eng-runtime after 1h with the first 5m numbers. :eyes:

jon: thanks all — good catch and fast iteration.
